findings: The o4 statement about fewer sensor readings and a faster servo is not uniformly false without a baseline sampling relationship. An initially oversampled sensor can be reduced from 1000 Hz to 500 Hz while the servo increases from 100 Hz to 200 Hz, still allowing fresh measurements every cycle. Specify one fresh measurement per original cycle with no surplus sampling, or replace o4 with a genuinely stale/reused-measurement misconception.
As written, o4 can describe a feasible oversampled-sensor configuration, so it is not a cleanly false alternative even though o1 remains the intended general source interpretation.

The explanation that fewer readings cannot provide fresh feedback at every faster cycle assumes an unstated baseline. Qualify that claim or change the alternative; do not teach a universal impossibility.

The answer and homogeneous matrix-coupling argument are correctly supported by page 735, but the attached formula introduces the full nonhomogeneous residual M qdd_d+h−tau_ff and h=V+G+F. Those premises require the plant on page 730 and controller architecture on page 734, as already cited by Q01. Either add those exact premise citations and explain the residual derivation, or narrow this formula record to the displayed homogeneous equation under the explicitly stated zero-residual approximation.

The formula combines a transient error-dynamics equation with a steady equilibrium relation, but defines M only as actual inertia at the equilibrium pose. The transient disturbance-sign question uses M(q(t)) at the current actual configuration; only the steady expression evaluates it at equilibrium. Define both scopes explicitly so the general dynamic equation is not silently frozen. The positive disturbance sign and current key are correct.
